discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computing and quantum simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum information and atomic physics theory
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned quantum computation from an abstract idea into concrete physics. Their 1995 proposal of a trapped-ion quantum computer, with entangling gates mediated by collective motion, gave the first realistic architecture and directly guided the experiments that produced the first quantum logic gates. Its principles still underlie today's ion-trap processors. They then showed how neutral atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models and controlled collisional entanglement. This established analog quantum simulation, which led to the observation of the superfluid–Mott insulator transition and a wide range of many-body experiments. Their ideas on quantum repeaters, quantum networks, and tensor-network descriptions of many-body states shaped quantum information science more broadly. Few theoretical contributions have been so precise, so quickly verified, and so lasting in their effect on experiments across atomic physics, condensed matter, and quantum technology.
